# #244 — The operator sees the run's legs from the run's own page

Tom's commitment item (first freed lane), ratified by Waffles 00:18Z with
the acceptance test verbatim, general go from Tom 01:54Z ("especially the
uncontroversial stuff... no cut corners"). Folds board #59 + the console
half of #107's gap. Ground truth: Waffles' operator-experience report §1
(docs/tracking/aion-operator-experience-20260815.md) — every defect line
below happened to a real operator tonight.

## The acceptance test (Waffles, verbatim — this is the red case)

"The operator watching a named fleet run must see its legs' live
transcripts from the run's own page without knowing child ids exist —
Tom tonight, verbatim, is the red case."

Tom watched K9's parent run page after fanout: event history ends at
ActivityStarted for hours (honestly quiet — nothing newer exists in that
store), while both builder legs streamed thousands of transcript events
under CHILD workflow ids he had no reason to know existed. He concluded
the system was broken. Nothing was broken. That gap is the defect.

## What exists (proven live tonight — build on it, don't rebuild it)

- Child ids ARE in the parent's event history: ChildWorkflowStarted
  events carry child_workflow_id. This is the derivation seam.
- Child transcripts DO flow mid-activity: POST /workflows/transcripts
  (list: namespace/workflow_id/run_id → streams with head) and POST
  /workflows/transcript (fetch: + activity_id/attempt/from_seq/limit)
  — proven advancing live on K9's L1/L2 (heads 2667→2759 measured).
- Streams are keyed 4-axis (workflow/run/activity/attempt) since #168;
  attempt is part of the key — surface it, don't collapse it (#246
  taught that attempt identity is operator-safety information).

## The build

R1 — **Server: derived children endpoint.** The parent run's page needs
"who are my children" answered server-side by DERIVING from the parent's
own event history (ChildWorkflowStarted → child workflow/run ids +
display names + status projection). NO schema change, NO stored
parent→children relation — that is #107, which sits on TOM'S DOCKET
gating ADR-004. **HARD WALL (Waffles 01:54Z): if the honest fix needs
the schema relation, STOP and bring the finding to the dispatcher —
never widen silently.** Depth: one level is what fleet_dev produces
today; recursion can derive iteratively if trivial, otherwise disclose
as a non-goal.

R2 — **Console: the run page folds its legs in.** On a run with
children: a legs section, one entry per child (display name, short id
beside it per the #211 law, status, current activity + attempt), each
tailing its live transcript through the existing transcript endpoints.
Live = the console's socket-first discipline (board law: real data
only, no polling theater where a socket exists). The parent's own quiet
history stays visible and honest — the legs section ANSWERS the quiet,
it doesn't hide it.

R3 — **CLI: the same answer at the terminal.** `aion tail <workflow-id>`
(report §1's shape): resolves the run, discovers legs via R1's
derivation, tails parent + child transcripts interleaved with leg
prefixes. Terminal operators get what the console gets — one story.

R4 — **Attempt honesty everywhere.** Wherever R2/R3 show a leg's
stream, the attempt number is visible, and a stream that went quiet
because its attempt was superseded says so rather than reading as
"working". (The #207 double-writer made this non-cosmetic.)

## Red-first discipline

The acceptance red is reproducible tonight: a fleet_dev parent with
running children whose parent page/CLI answer contains NO leg
information. Pin it: an e2e that starts a parent-with-children fixture,
asks the R1 endpoint / R3 verb, and asserts leg visibility — written
first, committed failing against the current tree, then built green.
Console side pins the legs section renders from a recorded fixture.

## Out of scope (disclosed non-goals)

- #107's schema-level parent→children relation (Tom's docket; the wall
  above).
- Heartbeats in run history (report §1 mentions them — separate line,
  needs engine-record design like #249).
- The one-surface observability redesign (report §6 — design
  conversation, not this build).
- Any landing/swap/restart while K9/#207 fly (standing wall; landed is
  not running).

## House laws

Worktree-only build, commit-as-you-go, never push. No #[allow]/
#[ignore]/lint bypasses. Files ≤500 LOC. Clippy ×2 resolutions + fmt +
battery to files. Waffles' re-gate before landing; his desk lands it.

Work from the current repository state. Return only the value required
by the supplied output schema. Do not claim completion or verification
without direct evidence.

1	//! Durable transcript read API (lane #229): the REST twin of the events pair.
2	//!
3	//! `POST /workflows/transcript` fetches the retained transcript of one
4	//! `(workflow, run, activity, attempt)` stream from the durable `O` keyspace,
5	//! and `POST /workflows/transcripts` enumerates one RUN's retained streams.
6	//!
7	//! Together they mirror the workflow-history pair: `/workflows/describe` is the
8	//! socket-free history read, the `/events/stream` subscription is the live
9	//! tail — and for transcripts this pair is the socket-free read while the
10	//! `/events/stream` transcript subscription remains the live-tail attach. A
11	//! client that wants both does a REST fetch first, then attaches the WS with
12	//! `after_seq` = the last fetched `store_seq` (the publisher's subscribe path
13	//! dedups the splice seam on `store_seq`).
14	//!
15	//! Both endpoints are namespace-scoped through the SAME per-workflow gate the
16	//! transcript WS subscription uses ([`gate_transcript_workflow`]), so a caller
17	//! probing a foreign or nonexistent workflow receives the guard's anti-leak
18	//! `not_found`, never a transcript. An authorized workflow with nothing
19	//! retained answers `200` with an empty list — the honest answer for an old
20	//! run recorded before retention existed, never an error.
21	//!
22	//! # The run axis is required on both requests
23	//!
24	//! A continue-as-new chain reuses one workflow id while activity ordinals and
25	//! attempt numbers restart in every generation, so a request naming only
26	//! `(workflow, activity, attempt)` does not identify a stream. `run_id` is
27	//! required rather than optional-with-a-latest-run-default, because a default
28	//! would answer a question the caller did not ask, and would do it silently.
29	
30	use aion_core::{ActivityEvent, ActivityId, RunId, WorkflowId};
31	use aion_proto::WireError;
32	use aion_store::{ActivityRecord, ActivityStreamKey};
33	use axum::{Json, extract::State};
34	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
35	
36	use super::auth::HttpCaller;
37	use super::error::HttpWireError;
38	use crate::ServerState;
39	use crate::stream::gate_transcript_workflow;
40	
41	const MAX_WINDOW_LIMIT: u32 = 2_000;
42	
43	/// The transcript-fetch request body: the target stream's full identity plus
44	/// the namespace the workflow runs under (the auth scope), an optional resume
45	/// cursor, and optional bounded-window selectors.
46	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
47	pub(crate) struct TranscriptFetchRequest {
48	    /// The namespace the target workflow runs under (the auth scope).
49	    pub namespace: String,
50	    /// The target workflow.
51	    pub workflow_id: WorkflowId,
52	    /// The target run of that workflow — the second stream axis. REQUIRED: two
53	    /// generations of one continue-as-new chain share every other coordinate.
54	    pub run_id: RunId,
55	    /// The target activity within the workflow.
56	    pub activity_id: ActivityId,
57	    /// The target attempt — the fourth stream axis.
58	    pub attempt: u32,
59	    /// Read records with `store_seq >= from_seq`; omitted reads the whole
60	    /// retained transcript from `store_seq == 0`.
61	    #[serde(default)]
62	    pub from_seq: Option<u64>,
63	    /// Maximum records to return. Omitted preserves the unbounded legacy read.
64	    #[serde(default)]
65	    pub limit: Option<u32>,
66	    /// Return only the last `n` retained records. Mutually exclusive with
67	    /// `from_seq`.
68	    #[serde(default)]
69	    pub last: Option<u32>,
70	}
71	
72	/// The transcript-fetch response body: the retained events, in `store_seq`
73	/// order, each carrying its `store_seq`. Empty for a stream with nothing
74	/// retained (an unknown or pre-retention run).
75	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
76	pub(crate) struct TranscriptFetchResponse {
77	    /// The retained transcript events in `store_seq` order.
78	    pub events: Vec<ActivityEvent>,
79	    /// First omitted `store_seq` when `limit` truncated the response.
80	    pub next_from_seq: Option<u64>,
81	    /// Stream head at read time: the next durable `store_seq`.
82	    pub head_seq: u64,
83	}
84	
85	/// The stream-enumeration request body: the workflow whose retained transcript
86	/// streams to list, plus the namespace it runs under (the auth scope).
87	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
88	pub(crate) struct TranscriptStreamsRequest {
89	    /// The namespace the target workflow runs under (the auth scope).
90	    pub namespace: String,
91	    /// The workflow whose retained transcript streams to enumerate.
92	    pub workflow_id: WorkflowId,
93	    /// The run of that workflow whose retained streams to enumerate. REQUIRED:
94	    /// enumerating a whole continue-as-new chain would return several
95	    /// generations' streams under pairwise-colliding coordinates.
96	    pub run_id: RunId,
97	}
98	
99	/// One retained transcript stream of the workflow run.
100	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
101	pub(crate) struct TranscriptStreamEntry {
102	    /// The run the stream belongs to. Echoed on every row so a row lifted out of
103	    /// the response still names its generation.
104	    pub run_id: RunId,
105	    /// The activity within the workflow.
106	    pub activity_id: ActivityId,
107	    /// The attempt number — the fourth stream axis.
108	    pub attempt: u32,
109	    /// Next `store_seq` to be written == count of retained records.
110	    pub head: u64,
111	}
112	
113	/// The stream-enumeration response body: every retained stream, ordered by
114	/// `(activity, attempt)`. Empty for a workflow with no retained transcript.
115	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
116	pub(crate) struct TranscriptStreamsResponse {
117	    /// The RUN's retained transcript streams.
118	    pub streams: Vec<TranscriptStreamEntry>,
119	}
120	
121	/// `POST /workflows/transcript`.
122	///
123	/// Namespace-gates the caller (byte-identical to the transcript WS
124	/// subscription), then reads the retained `O` tail of the addressed stream
125	/// from `from_seq` (default `0`). An unknown or pre-retention stream returns
126	/// `200` with empty `events`, a null `next_from_seq`, and `head_seq == 0` — the
127	/// honest answer, never an error; only an authorization failure or a store fault
128	/// is an HTTP error.
129	pub(crate) async fn fetch_transcript(
130	    State(state): State<ServerState>,
131	    HttpCaller(caller): HttpCaller,
132	    Json(request): Json<TranscriptFetchRequest>,
133	) -> Result<Json<TranscriptFetchResponse>, HttpWireError> {
134	    gate_transcript_workflow(&state, &caller, &request.namespace, &request.workflow_id)
135	        .await
136	        .map_err(|error| HttpWireError(error.to_wire_error()))?;
137	    if request.from_seq.is_some() && request.last.is_some() {
138	        return Err(HttpWireError(WireError::invalid_input(
139	            "transcript from_seq and last are mutually exclusive",
140	        )));
141	    }
142	    let key = ActivityStreamKey::new(
143	        request.workflow_id,
144	        request.run_id,
145	        request.activity_id,
146	        request.attempt,
147	    );
148	    let from_seq = request.from_seq.map_or(0, |seq| seq);
149	    let read_from = request.last.map_or(from_seq, |_last| 0);
150	    let ranged = state
151	        .transcript_publisher()
152	        .replay_from(&key, read_from)
153	        .await
154	        .map_err(|error| HttpWireError(crate::ServerError::from(error).to_wire_error()))?;
155	    let mut records = if ranged.is_empty() && read_from != 0 {
156	        state
157	            .transcript_publisher()
158	            .replay_from(&key, 0)
159	            .await
160	            .map_err(|error| HttpWireError(crate::ServerError::from(error).to_wire_error()))?
161	    } else {
162	        ranged
163	    };
164	    let head_seq = transcript_head(&records)?;
165	    if request.last.is_none() && read_from != 0 {
166	        records.retain(|record| record.store_seq >= read_from);
167	    }
168	    if let Some(last) = request.last {
169	        let last = usize::try_from(last).map_err(|error| {
170	            HttpWireError(WireError::invalid_input(format!(
171	                "transcript last is too large: {error}"
172	            )))
173	        })?;
174	        let first = records.len().saturating_sub(last);
175	        drop(records.drain(..first));
176	    }
177	    let limit = request
178	        .limit
179	        .map(|limit| limit.clamp(1, MAX_WINDOW_LIMIT) as usize);
180	    let next_from_seq = limit.and_then(|limit| records.get(limit).map(|record| record.store_seq));
181	    if let Some(limit) = limit {
182	        records.truncate(limit);
183	    }
184	    Ok(Json(TranscriptFetchResponse {
185	        events: records.into_iter().map(|record| record.event).collect(),
186	        next_from_seq,
187	        head_seq,
188	    }))
189	}
190	
191	/// The stream head implied by a read: one past the last record's `store_seq`,
192	/// or `0` for a stream with nothing retained.
193	///
194	/// Shared with the live describe join so both surfaces compute the head the
195	/// same way — a head that differed between two reads of one stream would be a
196	/// disagreement an operator could not resolve.
197	pub(crate) fn transcript_head(records: &[ActivityRecord]) -> Result<u64, HttpWireError> {
198	    records.last().map_or(Ok(0), |record| {
199	        record.store_seq.checked_add(1).ok_or_else(|| {
200	            HttpWireError(WireError::backend(
201	                "transcript store_seq exhausted the u64 sequence space",
202	            ))
203	        })
204	    })
205	}
206	
207	/// `POST /workflows/transcripts`.
208	///
209	/// Namespace-gates the caller (the same per-workflow gate), then enumerates the
210	/// addressed RUN's retained transcript streams from the durable `O` keyspace —
211	/// one generation, never the whole continue-as-new chain. A run with no retained
212	/// transcript answers `200 { "streams": [] }` — old runs simply have none.
213	pub(crate) async fn list_transcript_streams(
214	    State(state): State<ServerState>,
215	    HttpCaller(caller): HttpCaller,
216	    Json(request): Json<TranscriptStreamsRequest>,
217	) -> Result<Json<TranscriptStreamsResponse>, HttpWireError> {
218	    gate_transcript_workflow(&state, &caller, &request.namespace, &request.workflow_id)
219	        .await
220	        .map_err(|error| HttpWireError(error.to_wire_error()))?;
221	    let summaries = state
222	        .transcript_publisher()
223	        .list_streams(&request.workflow_id, &request.run_id)
224	        .await
225	        .map_err(|error| HttpWireError(crate::ServerError::from(error).to_wire_error()))?;
226	    Ok(Json(TranscriptStreamsResponse {
227	        streams: summaries
228	            .into_iter()
229	            .map(|summary| TranscriptStreamEntry {
230	                run_id: summary.key.run_id,
231	                activity_id: summary.key.activity_id,
232	                attempt: summary.key.attempt,
233	                head: summary.head,
234	            })
235	            .collect(),
236	    }))
237	}

2	
3	use std::collections::HashMap;

13	/// Metadata recorded with every workflow history event.
14	#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, ts_rs::TS, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
15	pub struct EventEnvelope {
16	    /// Monotonic sequence number within the owning workflow history.
17	    pub seq: u64,
18	    /// Recorded UTC timestamp for this event.
19	    ///
20	    /// This timestamp is the determinism source for `workflow.now`; replay must use the recorded
21	    /// value rather than consulting wall-clock time.
22	    pub recorded_at: DateTime<Utc>,
23	    /// Workflow history that owns this event.
24	    pub workflow_id: WorkflowId,
25	}
26	
27	/// The named default task queue: the single sanctioned fallback when no explicit task queue was
28	/// selected (no SDK-level selection exists yet — that is NSTQ-4) and the replay-safe decode value
29	/// for [`Event::ActivityScheduled`] events recorded before the `task_queue` field existed.
30	///
31	/// This is the canonical task-queue default for the whole workspace. `aion_store::DEFAULT_OUTBOX_ROUTE`
32	/// and `aion_server::worker::registry::DEFAULT_TASK_QUEUE` both alias/re-export this constant rather
33	/// than redeclaring the literal, so a history-derived task queue and an outbox-row-derived task queue
34	/// cannot drift.
35	pub const DEFAULT_TASK_QUEUE: &str = "default";
36	
37	/// serde default for [`Event::ActivityScheduled::task_queue`]: the named [`DEFAULT_TASK_QUEUE`].
38	///
39	/// Used by `#[serde(default = ...)]` so an old recorded history that has no `task_queue` on its
40	/// `ActivityScheduled` events decodes deterministically to `"default"`.
41	fn default_task_queue() -> String {
42	    String::from(DEFAULT_TASK_QUEUE)
43	}
44	
45	/// Sentinel `attempt` value for activity lifecycle events decoded from a history recorded BEFORE the
46	/// `attempt` field existed on [`Event::ActivityStarted`] / [`Event::ActivityCompleted`] /
47	/// [`Event::ActivityCancelled`] (NOI-0).
48	///
49	/// Activity attempts are **one-based** everywhere they are produced (see [`Event::ActivityFailed`]'s
50	/// `attempt`, which is documented "One-based activity attempt number", and the engine's
51	/// `FIRST_DELIVERY_ATTEMPT = 1`). A real attempt is therefore always `>= 1`, so `0` can never collide
52	/// with a genuine attempt: it is a distinguishable "legacy / unknown attempt" marker. Old histories
53	/// that predate the field decode to this sentinel via `#[serde(default = "legacy_activity_attempt")]`
54	/// — deterministically, never panicking, never differing run-to-run — while the compiler still forces
55	/// every LIVE construction site to supply the genuine one-based attempt (there is no blanket
56	/// `Default` on the variant).
57	const LEGACY_ACTIVITY_ATTEMPT: u32 = 0;
58	
59	/// serde default for the `attempt` field on the activity lifecycle events that gained it in NOI-0.
60	///
61	/// Returns [`LEGACY_ACTIVITY_ATTEMPT`] (`0`) so a history recorded before the field existed decodes
62	/// deterministically to the legacy/unknown sentinel rather than failing. See
63	/// [`LEGACY_ACTIVITY_ATTEMPT`] for why `0` is a safe distinguishable value under one-based attempts.
64	fn legacy_activity_attempt() -> u32 {
65	    LEGACY_ACTIVITY_ATTEMPT
66	}
67	
68	/// Search attribute name that records the task queue a workflow was STARTED on.
69	///
70	/// The server stamps this attribute durably in the SAME atomic append as
71	/// [`Event::WorkflowStarted`] (via [`Event::SearchAttributesUpdated`]) when the
72	/// start request selected a task queue — mirroring the `aion.namespace`
73	/// attribute that records the owning namespace. It is therefore part of
74	/// RECORDED HISTORY: recovery/replay re-derive the identical value, so an
75	/// activity that falls back to its workflow's start-time queue (#144) resolves
76	/// to the same queue on every replay. The attribute is absent when the start
77	/// did not select a queue (the legacy / "no selection anywhere" case).
78	///
79	/// This is the canonical name for the whole workspace;
80	/// `aion_server::TASK_QUEUE_ATTRIBUTE` re-exports it rather than redeclaring the
81	/// literal, so a history-derived start-time queue and the server's recorded
82	/// attribute cannot drift.
83	pub const START_TIME_TASK_QUEUE_ATTRIBUTE: &str = "aion.task_queue";
84	
85	/// The task queue a workflow was STARTED on, projected from recorded history.
86	///
87	/// Reads the [`START_TIME_TASK_QUEUE_ATTRIBUTE`] search attribute folded from
88	/// the run's [`Event::SearchAttributesUpdated`] events (the server records it in
89	/// the same append as [`Event::WorkflowStarted`]). Returns `None` when the start
90	/// recorded no task-queue selection — a legacy history, or a start that left the
91	/// queue unset — so callers fall back to the named [`DEFAULT_TASK_QUEUE`].
92	///
93	/// Because the value is read purely from recorded history (never from live or
94	/// wall-clock state), it is replay-deterministic: the same history always
95	/// projects the same start-time queue.
96	#[must_use]
97	pub fn start_time_task_queue(events: &[Event]) -> Option<String> {
98	    let attributes = crate::search_attributes_from_events(events);
99	    match attributes.get(START_TIME_TASK_QUEUE_ATTRIBUTE) {
100	        Some(crate::SearchAttributeValue::String(queue)) => Some(queue.clone()),
101	        _ => None,
102	    }
103	}
104	
105	/// Search attribute name that carries a workflow's operator-facing display
106	/// name (#211).
107	///
108	/// The display name is a LABEL over the workflow's UUID identity, never an
109	/// address. Stated exactly, because the label rule is about ACTS and not about
110	/// whether a name may appear on the wire:
111	///
112	/// 1. **No operation acts on a name.** Every act-verb — start, signal, query,
113	///    cancel, pause, resume, reopen, rename, intervene — takes a `WorkflowId`
114	///    (and optionally a `RunId`). None of them accepts a name as its target.
115	/// 2. **Name-shaped FILTERING returns lists and acts on nothing.** This
116	///    attribute is an ordinary search attribute, so it is filterable like any
117	///    other: a visibility predicate on it yields candidate summaries. That is
118	///    the first half of a picker (name in, candidates out, an operator
119	///    chooses, a UUID acts), and it is deliberately supported.
120	/// 3. **The composition is prohibited.** No SDK, CLI verb, MCP tool, or
121	///    convenience function may compose name-filter → take-first → act. That
122	///    composition re-imports addressing one layer up: the system, not the
123	///    caller, would be choosing the referent. The CHOOSING STEP STAYS WITH THE
124	///    CALLER, BY CONTRACT. A future "find by name" helper RETURNS CANDIDATES
125	///    AND STOPS.
126	///
127	/// The sweep predicate, written down so the next audit checks the right thing
128	/// rather than re-deriving it: *for every verb, HTTP route, RPC, MCP tool, and
129	/// SDK function that CHANGES state, the target is identified by a UUID; a
130	/// display name appears only as a value being SET, never as the selector, and
131	/// no single call turns a name into an act.* The MCP tool catalogue enforces
132	/// this mechanically (`aion_server::mcp::catalog` — see its
133	/// `name_is_not_an_address_tests`); the other surfaces are Rust types rather
134	/// than data and are checked by reading against that predicate.
135	///
136	/// It is recorded durably as an ordinary [`Event::SearchAttributesUpdated`]
137	/// search attribute — stamped in the same atomic append as
138	/// [`Event::WorkflowStarted`] when the start named one, and re-recorded by
139	/// every rename — so history keeps every name the workflow has worn and
140	/// replay/failover re-derive the current one.
141	///
142	/// The recorded attribute carries NO run id. A rename is addressed to a
143	/// workflow AND a run, but what it records is a workflow-level attribute, and
144	/// every reader folds it over the whole history (see [`display_name`]). So a
145	/// continue-as-new successor inherits the name its predecessor was wearing, and
146	/// describing any run of the workflow reads back the same, current name.
147	///
148	/// This is the canonical name for the whole workspace;
149	/// `aion_server::DISPLAY_NAME_ATTRIBUTE` re-exports it rather than redeclaring
150	/// the literal, so the projector below and the server's recorded attribute
151	/// cannot drift.
152	pub const DISPLAY_NAME_ATTRIBUTE: &str = "aion.display_name";
153	
154	/// The workflow's current display name, projected from recorded history.
155	///
156	/// Reads the [`DISPLAY_NAME_ATTRIBUTE`] search attribute folded over EVERY
157	/// [`Event::SearchAttributesUpdated`] in `events`, last write wins — so a
158	/// rename's later update supersedes the start-time name while history keeps
159	/// both. Returns `None` when no name was ever recorded (the unnamed workflow
160	/// renders as its bare UUID).
161	///
162	/// The fold is per WORKFLOW, not per run: it is not run-scoped the way
163	/// [`crate::failure_projection`] and [`crate::current_lease_terminal`] are, and
164	/// the recorded attribute carries no run id to scope it by. Hand it a whole
165	/// workflow history and the newest recorded name wins whichever run recorded
166	/// it — so a continue-as-new successor reads back the name its predecessor was
167	/// wearing until something renames it.
168	///
169	/// Because the value is read purely from recorded history (never from live or
170	/// wall-clock state), it is replay-deterministic: the same history always
171	/// projects the same display name.
172	#[must_use]
173	pub fn display_name(events: &[Event]) -> Option<String> {
174	    display_name_from_attributes(&crate::search_attributes_from_events(events))
175	}
176	
177	/// The display name carried by an already-folded search-attribute map.
178	///
179	/// The same projection as [`display_name`], for readers that hold the folded
180	/// map rather than the events — the visibility projection's
181	/// `search_attributes`, which the store keeps refreshed on every append. Both
182	/// entry points share this one lookup so the attribute name and the
183	/// String-typed expectation cannot drift between the history reader and the
184	/// visibility reader. The map is itself folded over a whole workflow history,
185	/// so this reads the same per-workflow label with the same last-write-wins
186	/// rule.
187	#[must_use]
188	pub fn display_name_from_attributes<S: std::hash::BuildHasher>(
189	    attributes: &std::collections::HashMap<String, crate::SearchAttributeValue, S>,
190	) -> Option<String> {
191	    match attributes.get(DISPLAY_NAME_ATTRIBUTE) {
192	        Some(crate::SearchAttributeValue::String(name)) => Some(name.clone()),
193	        _ => None,
194	    }
195	}

198	///
199	/// User data is carried as opaque [`Payload`] values, while failures use the closed workflow and

227	        /// Opaque workflow result payload.

234	        /// Terminal workflow failure.

241	        /// Human-readable cancellation reason.
242	        reason: String,
243	    },
244	    /// A workflow execution timed out; this terminal event projects to `TimedOut`.
245	    WorkflowTimedOut {
246	        /// Recording metadata for this event.
247	        envelope: EventEnvelope,
248	        /// Descriptor identifying the timeout that elapsed.

1	//! The `aion` command line: workflow operations over gRPC and the embedded
2	//! Aion workflow server (`aion server`).
3	
4	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
5	use std::process::ExitCode;
6	use std::time::Duration;
7	
8	use aion_client::{Client, ClientBuilder, ClientError, ListPage};
9	use aion_core::{Payload, WorkflowFilter, WorkflowStatus};
10	use anyhow::{Context, Result};
11	use clap::{Parser, Subcommand};
12	use serde_json::Value;
13	
14	use crate::output::{
15	    AcknowledgementOutput, QueryOutput, describe_output, pause_output, print_json, reopen_output,
16	    resume_output, to_value,
17	};

19	    json_payload, parse_run_id, parse_status, parse_workflow_id, payload_to_json,
20	};

51	const DEFAULT_ENDPOINT: &str = "127.0.0.1:50051";
52	const DEFAULT_NAMESPACE: &str = "default";
53	const DEFAULT_SUBJECT: &str = "cli-user";
54	const QUERY_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);
55	
56	/// Aion workflow command line.
57	#[derive(Debug, Parser)]
58	#[command(
59	    name = "aion",
60	    version,
61	    about = "Operate Aion workflows over gRPC and run the Aion workflow server. \
62	             Bare `aion` starts the server in the background and opens the ops console."
63	)]
64	struct Cli {
65	    /// gRPC server endpoint a client dials. A missing scheme is interpreted as
66	    /// http://. Not a bind address: `aion server` takes `--grpc-address`.
67	    ///
68	    /// Deliberately has no clap `default_value`, so the difference between
69	    /// "the operator named an endpoint" and "nobody said" survives parsing.
70	    /// `aion server` needs that difference to refuse a flag it cannot honour;
71	    /// a default applied here would erase it before anyone could ask.
72	    #[arg(long, global = true)]
73	    endpoint: Option<String>,
74	    /// Workflow namespace used for operations.
75	    #[arg(long, global = true, default_value = DEFAULT_NAMESPACE)]
76	    namespace: String,
77	    /// Caller subject metadata sent to the server.
78	    #[arg(long, global = true, default_value = DEFAULT_SUBJECT)]
79	    subject: String,
80	    /// Bearer token for authenticated servers. Overrides the `AION_TOKEN`
81	    /// environment variable; when both are absent the development
82	    /// header paths apply.
83	    #[arg(long, global = true)]
84	    token: Option<String>,
85	    /// Print formatted, human-readable JSON.
86	    #[arg(long, global = true)]
87	    pretty: bool,
88	    /// Bare `aion` only: run the launched server in this terminal instead of
89	    /// the background.
90	    #[arg(long)]
91	    foreground: bool,
92	    /// Bare `aion` only: do not open the ops console in a browser.
93	    #[arg(long)]
94	    no_open: bool,
95	    /// Absent means the bare launcher: start the server in the background,
96	    /// wait until it is live, report in plain language, open the console.
97	    #[command(subcommand)]
98	    command: Option<Command>,
99	}
100	
101	#[derive(Debug, Subcommand)]
102	enum Command {
103	    /// Run the Aion workflow server (HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, remote workers).
104	    ///
105	    /// Loads configuration from `--config`, the environment, and command-line
106	    /// overrides, serves until a termination signal arrives, then drains
107	    /// in-flight activities gracefully before exiting.
108	    Server(server::ServerArgs),
109	    /// The instant authoring loop: watch a workflow project and hot-load on save.
110	    ///
111	    /// Watches the project's `src/` tree and, on every save, rebuilds and
112	    /// type-checks it through the external `gleam` binary, repackages it into a
113	    /// content-hash-versioned `.aion`, and hot-loads that version into the
114	    /// running server named by `--endpoint` — with no engine restart. A run
115	    /// already in-flight keeps executing on the immutable version it started
116	    /// with; only fresh runs pick up the reload. The `gleam` binary path is
117	    /// required (`--gleam-path`); there is no default. An optional
118	    /// `--debounce-ms` coalesces an editor's multi-event save into one rebuild.
119	    Dev(dev::DevArgs),
120	    /// Author AWL workflow documents (rev-2 surface): check, format, emit
121	    /// Gleam, derive JSON Schema, and read the language's own guide.
122	    ///
123	    /// Runs entirely locally and never connects to a server. `check` parses
124	    /// and typechecks a document, printing compiler-style
125	    /// `<file>:<line>:<column>: error: <message>` diagnostics to stderr;
126	    /// `fmt` rewrites the document in place with the canonical printer (the
127	    /// printer is the formatter — there is no check mode); `emit` lowers a
128	    /// checked document to a Gleam workflow module (the stopgap execution
129	    /// target); `schema` derives draft 2020-12 JSON Schema from the same
130	    /// checked document; `guide` prints what any word of the language means.
131	    ///
132	    /// The documents behind this surface, all in the repository:
133	    /// `docs/authoring/AWL.md` introduces the language and the loop;
134	    /// `examples/assistant/resources/AWL-REFERENCE.md` is the complete
135	    /// reference every `guide` entry cites by section;
136	    /// `examples/assistant/resources/AWL-AUTHORING.md` walks from an
137	    /// objective to a checked document;
138	    /// `examples/assistant/resources/WORKERS.md` says what actually serves a
139	    /// declared action; `examples/assistant/resources/COMMANDS.md` covers
140	    /// every command in this loop with its failure modes; and
141	    /// `docs/workers/DECLARED-COMMANDS.md` must be read before writing a
142	    /// `run "…"` body, because there is no sandbox.
143	    Awl {
144	        #[command(subcommand)]
145	        command: awl::AwlCommand,
146	    },
147	    /// Run worker processes supplied by the Aion distribution.
148	    Worker {
149	        #[command(subcommand)]
150	        command: WorkerCommand,
151	    },
152	    /// Operate the assistant that ships inside this binary.
153	    ///
154	    /// The assistant document is compiled into `aion` itself and installed by
155	    /// `aion server` on a home that holds no version of it, so a fresh install
156	    /// has an assistant with no deploy step. `document` and `describe` read the
157	    /// binary; `start`, `say`, `end`, and `status` drive a session on the
158	    /// server named by `--endpoint`. Serving the agent action a session
159	    /// dispatches is still a worker's job (`aion worker agent`).
160	    Assistant {
161	        #[command(subcommand)]
162	        command: assistant::AssistantCommand,
163	    },
164	    /// Operate a running Aion server or package workflows locally.
165	    #[command(flatten)]
166	    Client(ClientCommand),
167	}
168	
169	#[derive(Debug, Subcommand)]
170	enum WorkerCommand {
171	    /// Serve strict manifest-wired shell commands on an Aion task queue.

607	/// flags on `aion worker awl` (see [`crate::worker_awl::args`], and the start command
608	/// `docs/workers/AWL-WORKER-DOCUMENTS.md` publishes). An operator who mistypes that
609	/// documented line must not be told those flags are deleted and sent to write a `harness`
610	/// section — a worker-family document is FORBIDDEN to carry one, because every action in
611	/// it has a declared body and there is nothing for an agent to serve. That advice would
612	/// send them to a refusal, from a refusal, for a flag that was never wrong.
613	const MIGRATED_FLAG_VERB: [&str; 2] = ["worker", "agent"];

670	         The record is the thing to fix: add the `harness` section to the document, then \
671	         re-mint the deployment (`PUT /worker-deployments/<name>`, or the ops console's deploy \
672	         form) so its stored argv no longer carries these flags."
673	    ))

151	/// Per-workflow transcript gate shared by the WS subscription and the REST
152	/// fetch/enumeration endpoints — byte-identical to the workflow event
153	/// subscription's authorization: the caller must hold a grant for `namespace`
154	/// AND `workflow_id` must be visible in it (anti-leak `not_found` otherwise).
155	pub(crate) async fn gate_transcript_workflow(
156	    state: &ServerState,
157	    caller: &CallerIdentity,
158	    namespace: &str,
159	    workflow_id: &aion_core::WorkflowId,
160	) -> Result<(), ServerError> {
161	    let per_workflow = PerWorkflowSubscription {
162	        namespace: namespace.to_owned(),
163	        workflow_id: Some(ProtoWorkflowId::from(workflow_id.clone())),
164	        resume_from_seq: None,
165	    };
166	    let target = WorkflowTarget::workflow(workflow_id);
167	    let scope = SubscriptionScope::PerWorkflow(&per_workflow, target);
168	    let filter = aion::EventFilter {
169	        workflow_id: Some(workflow_id.clone()),
170	        ..aion::EventFilter::default()
171	    };
172	    let operation = NamespaceOperation::subscribe(scope, &filter);
173	    // Guard verdict FIRST: nothing runs for an unauthorized caller. The scoped
174	    // engine handle is not needed here — transcripts read the `O` keyspace
175	    // through the publisher, never the engine.
176	    let scoped = state.namespace_guard().scope(caller, &operation).await?;
177	    drop(scoped);
178	    Ok(())
179	}

181	/// A live transcript event for one `(workflow, run, activity, attempt)` produced by an agent
182	/// harness.
183	///
184	/// Streamed to the ops console in real time and persisted to a durable observability keyspace
185	/// (except [`Self::ephemeral`] events). It is **never** mixed into workflow replay history — the
186	/// activity's single terminal result is the replay-authoritative output, not this transcript.
187	///
188	/// # The run axis is REQUIRED, not optional
189	///
190	/// A continue-as-new chain reuses one [`WorkflowId`] across generations while activity ordinals
191	/// restart at `0` and attempts restart at `1` in each new run. Without [`Self::run_id`] two
192	/// generations of one chain produce byte-identical stream identities, and their transcripts fuse:
193	/// generation two's first event lands on generation one's stream head. `run_id` is therefore a
194	/// plain required field — an `Option` would let the ambiguity back in through the `None` arm, and
195	/// there is no honest value to default it to. The same law already holds one layer over, where
196	/// the activity idempotency key is run-scoped over the identical triple.
197	///
198	/// # Ordering
199	///
200	/// [`Self::emitted_at`] and [`Self::worker_seq`] are best-effort producer-side ordering hints.
201	/// [`Self::store_seq`] is assigned by the server at durable-commit time and is `None` until the
202	/// event has been persisted — an unpersisted (e.g. ephemeral, or in-flight) event carries no
203	/// store sequence.
204	#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, ts_rs::TS, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
205	pub struct ActivityEvent {
206	    /// The workflow this activity belongs to.
207	    pub workflow_id: WorkflowId,
208	    /// The concrete run of that workflow this event was produced in — the second stream axis.
209	    ///
210	    /// Required. Two generations of one continue-as-new chain share a `workflow_id` and restart
211	    /// their ordinals and attempts, so this is the only field that keeps their transcripts apart.
212	    pub run_id: RunId,
213	    /// The activity within the workflow.
214	    pub activity_id: ActivityId,
215	    /// The attempt number of the activity this event was produced during.
216	    pub attempt: u32,
217	    /// Sub-identity of the agent that produced this event — REQUIRED for multi-agent
218	    /// attribution (a single activity attempt may run several agents).
219	    pub agent_id: Uuid,
220	    /// The role/label of the producing agent (e.g. an orchestrator vs a sub-agent).
221	    pub agent_role: String,
222	    /// Producer-clock instant the event was emitted (best-effort ordering hint).
223	    pub emitted_at: DateTime<Utc>,
224	    /// Worker-local best-effort monotonic sequence.
225	    ///
226	    /// Exported to TypeScript as `number`; see the module docs for the accepted `2^53` ceiling.
227	    pub worker_seq: u64,
228	    /// Server-stamped monotonic sequence assigned at durable-commit time; `None` until the event
229	    /// is persisted (ephemeral events are never persisted and always carry `None`).
230	    ///
231	    /// Exported to TypeScript as `number`; see the module docs for the accepted `2^53` ceiling.
232	    pub store_seq: Option<u64>,
233	    /// When `true`, this event is WS-forward-only and is **never persisted** (token deltas).
234	    pub ephemeral: bool,
235	    /// The classified payload of this event.
236	    pub kind: ActivityEventKind,
237	}

1010	    match input_file {

1016	        }
1017	        None => json_payload(input).context("invalid --input JSON"),
1018	    }
1019	}

250	/// listener. It is dark unless `[mcp].enabled` is set, and a dark surface is a
251	/// plain 404 — indistinguishable from a build that never had the route.
252	///
253	/// A construction failure (a published tool schema that will not compile) is
254	/// NOT downgraded to a dark surface: it is a server defect, and an operator who
255	/// asked for the endpoint would otherwise get a 404 and no idea why.
256	///
257	/// Each call builds one runtime, and a runtime owns one task store. That is
258	/// correct because a task is reachable only through the identifier its creator
259	/// was handed: two routers are two disjoint sets of handles, never a split view
260	/// of one set. The serving path builds the router exactly once.
261	fn mcp_family(state: &ServerState) -> Result<Router<ServerState>, ServerError> {
262	    if !state.runtime_config().mcp.enabled {
263	        return Ok(mcp_disabled_router());
264	    }
265	    let runtime = McpRuntime::build(state.clone(), &state.runtime_config().mcp)?;
266	    Ok(mcp_router(std::sync::Arc::new(runtime)))
267	}

269	/// Build the public workflow-management HTTP router.
270	pub fn workflow_router(state: ServerState) -> Router {
271	    // The deploy surface is dark by default: when `[deploy].enabled` is
272	    // false the routes are not mounted and every `/deploy/*` path is a
273	    // plain 404 (the explicit catch-all keeps the ops-console SPA fallback
274	    // from answering for the deploy namespace). The archive upload route
275	    // disables the default body limit because `read_archive_body` enforces
276	    // the operator-configured `deploy.max_archive_bytes` ceiling while
277	    // streaming.
278	    let deploy = if state.runtime_config().deploy.enabled {
279	        Router::new()
280	            .route(
281	                "/deploy/packages",
282	                post(upload_package).layer(DefaultBodyLimit::disable()),
283	            )
284	            .route("/deploy/versions", get(list_versions))
285	            .route("/deploy/route", post(route_version))
286	            .route("/deploy/unload", post(unload_version))
287	    } else {
288	        Router::new().route("/deploy/{*rest}", any(deploy_disabled))
289	    };
290	    // The authoring surface is dark by default, gated on
291	    // `[authoring].gleam_path`: when it is unset the routes are not mounted and
292	    // every `/authoring/*` path is a plain 404 (the explicit catch-all keeps
293	    // the ops-console SPA fallback from answering for the authoring namespace).

summary.text: **Confirming test results and partial e2e status**

arguments.summary: Implemented one-level child-workflow visibility end to end. The server now derives named child legs from authoritative parent/child histories; the run page discovers and socket-tails each leg without polling; and `aion tail <parent-workflow-id>` backfills and interleaves parent/child transcripts while preserving run, activity, attempt, and supersession identity. Changes are committed in eight cohesive commits and the worktree is clean.

changes.description: Added the namespace-authorized children projection endpoint, with explicit/latest parent-run resolution and derived child display name, run, lifecycle status, and current activity attempt.
Added the red-first recorded-history acceptance fixture covering explicit and latest-run child derivation.
Made the existing authorized namespace engine lookup reusable within HTTP handlers.
Registered the children handler and regression fixture modules.
Mounted the child projection route and extracted cohesive route/test sections to remain within repository lint limits.
Moved the existing router tests into their own module without changing their behavior.
Added the typed authenticated children REST client contract.
Exported child-leg API types and reader.
Added configured child-reader construction using the console's existing endpoint and credential plumbing.
Exported the configured child reader.
Added non-polling child discovery; live parent ChildWorkflowStarted sequence changes trigger a single derived reread.
Added the run-page Legs section with short child IDs, display names, status/current attempt, live per-child sockets, transcript rendering, and explicit superseded-attempt labels.
Integrated child legs beneath the existing parent history and wired already-open pages to discover fanout from live parent events.
Added a recorded-fixture regression for child identity, status, current attempt, transcript content, and supersession honesty.
Implemented parent-run resolution, child discovery, retained transcript backfill, readable identity prefixes, interleaving, snapshot mode, and live socket following.
Added socket-driven successor-attempt discovery so prior attempts are marked superseded and new transcript sockets are opened without polling.
Added `aion tail <workflow-id>` with optional run/HTTP endpoint/snapshot controls, existing auth and namespace propagation, and parser classification coverage.
Added workspace-pinned HTTP, stream, and WebSocket dependencies needed by tail.
Recorded the CLI dependency resolution changes.

verification.command: cargo test -p aion-server parent_run_derives_its_visible_leg_from_recorded_history --lib && cargo test -p aion-cli --no-default-features --features libsql-backend tail
verification.evidence: Server acceptance: 1 passed, 0 failed. CLI focused suite: 7 relevant unit tests plus existing filtered integration matches passed; coverage includes parent-only tail parsing, attempt labels, and highest-attempt selection.

verification.command: cd apps/aion-ops-console && bun run check && bun run typecheck && bun test && bun run build
verification.evidence: Biome exited 0 with two pre-existing complexity warnings; TypeScript passed; 1006 tests passed with 0 failures; Vite production build completed successfully.
Default-feature clippy completed successfully after production/test source decomposition; no lint suppressions were added.

The slim matrix reaches unrelated pre-existing feature-shape failures: feature-gated LivenessProbe is imported by grpc_worker_liveness_e2e without liminal-transport, no-harness CLI tests become unreachable/never-loop, and existing slim-only state/registry clippy diagnostics fire. The feature implementation itself compiles and its focused CLI tests pass under this resolution.
Rust formatting check exited 0 on the final committed tree.

verification.command: cargo test -p aion-rs -p aion-awl -p aion-awl-package -p aion-package -p aion-core
verification.evidence: The standard Rust battery stopped at existing `aion-awl-package --test sdk_closure_freshness`: 11 passed and `committed_closure_matches_a_fresh_oracle_harvest` failed because committed `aion@agent` BEAM chunks lag a fresh toolchain harvest.
Final output is only `## 244-child-visibility`; no uncommitted or untracked changes remain.

remaining_work: Repository baseline: regenerate and commit the AWL SDK closure with `scripts/regen-awl-sdk-closure.sh` to clear the unrelated freshness battery failure.

Repository baseline: repair the pre-existing no-default/libSQL all-target feature matrix (feature-gate liminal-only tests and resolve no-harness/slim clippy findings) before treating that matrix as a required green gate.
session_notes: The behavioral contract is intentionally one-level: callers identify only the parent workflow/run; child IDs and runs are derived from durable ChildWorkflowStarted history, while transcript and workflow sockets provide live delivery without polling.
Explicit run selection remains authoritative for CLI use; omission asks the server to resolve the latest recorded parent run for the current-run console page.
